## What this package does

The City of Windsor open data portal is an ArcGIS Hub site, backed by the
City's own ArcGIS Server at `mappmycity.ca`. There is no Windsor specific
R package on CRAN, so this package is a thin wrapper around
`arcgislayers::arc_read()`. It knows the Windsor catalogue, so you do not
have to type a full ArcGIS REST URL every time.

```{r}
library(windsoropendata)
```

## Install

On Windows, install the released dependencies from CRAN first, then the
package from GitHub:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages("arcgis")
# install.packages("pak")
pak::pak("durraniu/windsoropendata")
```

On Linux, the full `arcgis` metapackage can fail to compile its
`arcgisplaces` dependency (it needs Rust and OpenSSL headers). If that
happens, install just what this package needs:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
install.packages(c("arcgislayers", "dplyr", "httr2", "jsonlite", "tibble", "tidyr"))
pak::pak("durraniu/windsoropendata")
```

## List what is available

`windsor_datasets()` returns one row per dataset in the portal. The
package ships with a snapshot taken on 2026-11-10, with 227 datasets
across 9 services.

```{r}
datasets <- windsor_datasets()
nrow(datasets)
head(datasets[, c("dataset", "title", "service", "type", "geometry_type")])
```

`windsor_services()` summarises the 9 services:

```{r}
windsor_services()
```

To get the live catalogue instead of the snapshot, use
`windsor_datasets(refresh = TRUE)`. If the live fetch fails, you get the
snapshot back with a warning.

## Find a dataset

`windsor_search()` matches on a word in the dataset name, title or
service. It matches on a word boundary, so `"ward"` finds the ward
boundary but not `forward_sortation_area`.

```{r}
windsor_search("ward")
windsor_search("trail")
windsor_search("bike", service = "transportation")
```

## Read a dataset by name

`windsor_get()` looks up the short name and reads it with
`arcgislayers::arc_read()`. Spatial data comes back as an `sf` object in
EPSG 26917 (NAD 1983 UTM Zone 17N), the City's native projection.

### Ward boundaries

```{r}
wards <- windsor_get("ward_boundaries")
nrow(wards)
names(wards)
wards[, c("ward_number", "councillor_name")]
```

You can use the exact layer name, the title, or an alias. All three of
these read the same layer:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
windsor_get("municipal_ward_boundary")
windsor_get("Ward Boundaries")
windsor_get("wards")
```

### Peche Island Pathway

```{r}
peche <- windsor_get("peche_island_pathway")
nrow(peche)
peche[, c("trail_name", "trail_type", "status", "Shape_Length")]
sum(peche$Shape_Length)
```

The three segments total about 2,501 metres.

### Street centreline, preview first

The street centreline layer is large, with 6,312 features. Preview it
with `n_max` before reading the whole thing:

```{r}
streets <- windsor_get("street_centreline", n_max = 5)
streets[, c("street_name", "from_street", "to_street", "speed_limit", "lane_count")]
```

Then read it in full when you need it:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
streets <- windsor_get("street_centreline")
```

## Plot what you read

The result is an ordinary `sf` object, so it works with `ggplot2`,
`sf::plot()` and the rest of the tidyverse.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
library(ggplot2)
ggplot(wards) +
  geom_sf(aes(fill = factor(ward_number))) +
  theme_minimal()
```

## Windsor Police incidents

`windsor_police_incidents()` reads police-reported incidents from the
Windsor Police Service Incident Dashboard. This is a separate source
from the City open data portal: a public ArcGIS FeatureServer hosted by
Windsor Police Service, not one of the 227 datasets above. It covers
Windsor and Amherstburg for the last two years. Locations are
anonymised to the block, and motor vehicle collisions are not included.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
incidents <- windsor_police_incidents(n_max = 5)
traffic <- windsor_police_incidents(category = "Traffic", n_max = 5)
recent <- windsor_police_incidents(start_date = "2026-11-01", end_date = "2026-11-10")
```

`category` takes one or more of the 17 categories from
`windsor_police_categories()`. Dates are inclusive, and are
interpreted in the America/Toronto timezone, so `start_date =
"2026-11-01"` means incidents on 1 November in Windsor, not 1 November
in UTC. The result is an `sf` object in EPSG 26917, sorted by incident
date and time, so it joins directly to the ward boundaries above.

## Live traffic speeds and incidents from TomTom

The City portal publishes no measured speed or crash data. For live
measured speeds and incidents, `windsor_tomtom_flow()` and
`windsor_tomtom_incidents()` use the TomTom Traffic API instead. This
is a separate commercial source, not part of the City portal, and it
needs a free TomTom API key. Get one at
<https://developer.tomtom.com/> (no credit card), then set it:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
Sys.setenv(TOMTOM_API_KEY = "your-key")
```

`windsor_tomtom_flow()` returns the current speed and the free flow
speed for the road segment closest to each point, in km/h, with a
confidence score. Each point costs one TomTom API call, so keep the
number of points small when polling often.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
# Downtown Windsor, Ouellette Ave at Wyandotte St
windsor_tomtom_flow(lat = 42.318, lon = -83.039)

# Several points at once
windsor_tomtom_flow(
  lat = c(42.318, 42.300, 42.280),
  lon = c(-83.039, -83.000, -82.970)
)
```

`windsor_tomtom_incidents()` returns all current traffic incidents
in Windsor by default, as an `sf` object in EPSG 4326, with one row
per incident, a point or line geometry, and the delay and description.
Use `category` to filter, for example `"Accident"`, and see
`windsor_tomtom_categories()` for the full list of 13 categories.
`windsor_tomtom_bbox()` returns the default Windsor bounding box.

```{r, eval = FALSE}
windsor_tomtom_incidents()
windsor_tomtom_incidents(category = "Accident")
windsor_tomtom_categories()
```

TomTom incidents are live traffic events, not police collision
records, and TomTom data is not stored or redistributed by this
package.

## Ambiguous names

Three names are used by more than one service: `hydrant`,
`electric_vehicle_charger` and `public_property_obstruction`. For those,
add `service`:

```{r, eval = FALSE}
windsor_get("hydrant", service = "infrastructure")
windsor_get("hydrant", service = "governmentservices")
```

If you give an ambiguous name without a service, the error lists the
matches so you can pick one.

## Where the data comes from

* Portal: <https://open-data-portal-citywindsor.hub.arcgis.com/>
* REST services: <https://mappmycity.ca/arcgis/rest/services/open_data_services>
* Licence: the datasets are listed under Creative Commons Attribution
  4.0 International (CC BY 4.0).

`mappmycity.ca` is the City of Windsor's own ArcGIS Server, so the city
is in the server name, not in the URL path. A different city's server
with the same path would return that city's data.
